octor

R tools for the octo L1 larva connectome in CAVE (zlatic_octo-2_datastack), a SeaTable table of neuron seeds, and the Seymour L1 larva in CATMAID.

  • keep supervoxel and root IDs in SeaTable current, and flag neurons seeded more than once
  • find neurons by cell type and read their meshes (simplified for fast plotting)
  • query synapses, or download all synapse positions
  • transform neurons between Seymour and octo (landmarks + synapse-cloud registration)

Installation

octor lives in a private repository. To install it you need read access (ask the repository owner to add you as a collaborator) and a GitHub token:

install.packages(c("remotes", "usethis", "gitcreds"))
usethis::create_github_token()   # tick the "repo" scope, generate, copy the token
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()         # paste the token when asked
remotes::install_github("eichlerkathi/octor")

Use a classic token. Fine-grained tokens often cannot read private repositories owned by another account.

Setup

1. Python

octor talks to CAVE, SeaTable and CloudVolume through Python (via reticulate). Install the Python packages once:

octor::octo_python_setup()

If you have the natverse package fafbseg installed, this uses fafbseg::simple_python(), so octor shares the natverse Python environment. Otherwise octor creates its own environment and prints a RETICULATE_PYTHON=... line to add to ~/.Renviron.

Restart R afterwards.

2. CAVE token 

library(octor)
octo_get_token()

This opens the token page of the octo CAVE server in your browser. Log in, copy your token and paste it into the R console. octor checks that the token works and saves it as CAVE_TOKEN_BRAININBRAIN in ~/.Renviron, so you only do this once. Tokens for other CAVE datasets are not affected.

If you have no token yet, use octo_get_token(new = TRUE).

3. SeaTable token

In SeaTable, open the base, then ? menu ? Advanced ? API Token and create a token with read-write permission. Add it to ~/.Renviron (open the file with usethis::edit_r_environ()):

SEATABLE_API_TOKEN=<API token of the SeaTable base>

Restart R.

4. Check 

library(octor)
octo_python_check()   # Python and packages
octo_find_ids("KC")   # SeaTable connection

Troubleshooting

  • R uses the wrong Python: reticulate picks its Python once per session. Set RETICULATE_PYTHON=/path/to/python in ~/.Renviron and restart R.
  • Mesh or synapse results look like Python objects instead of R data: update reticulate (install.packages("reticulate")); numpy 2 needs reticulate 1.38 or newer.
  • Token rejected: run octo_get_token() again; tokens can expire.

Settings

Defaults are set as R options. To change one, e.g. in ~/.Rprofile:

options(octor.seatable_table = "Seeds",
        octor.seatable_url   = "https://cloud.seatable.io",
        octor.seymour_reg    = "~/data/seymour_octo_reg.rds")

See ?octor for all options.

Usage

SeaTable seeds 

octo_update_ids()                 # supervoxels, root IDs, double-seed flags
seeds <- octo_seeds(trusted_only = TRUE)

The seed table needs these columns: position (Text, Spelunker voxel coordinates), supervoxel_id, root_id, root_id_previous, dup_status and same_as (Text), root_changed_on and ids_checked_on (Date), n_seeds (Number) and primary (Checkbox). Keep the ID columns as Text: Number columns corrupt 64-bit IDs.

Neurons with several seeds share a root ID. In each group, tick primary on the row you trust. If no row is ticked, the row with the most annotation filled in is picked. A SeaTable view filtered on n_seeds > 1 and grouped by root_id shows the groups together.

Meshes 

ids <- octo_find_ids("^MBON")             # regex on cell_type
nl  <- octo_read_meshes(ids)              # 10% of faces by default
nl[, c("cell_type", "soma_side")]
rgl::plot3d(nl)

Synapses 

syn <- octo_synapses(pre = ids)           # needs a materialized datastack
pos <- octo_synapse_positions()           # all positions, no root IDs, resumable

Seymour → octo 

library(catmaid)
conn <- catmaid_login(server = ..., token = ...)
nl <- read_seymour_neurons("annotation:^MBON$", conn = conn)
nl_octo <- seymour2octo(nl)               # skeletons + connectors, nm

The registration file (about 60 MB) is not in the package. Get it at: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NJ-pJxH3CVPlpYD6es03B_MLNaUVh44h/view?usp=sharing, point options(octor.seymour_reg = ...) to it (a file path or a URL), or fit your own:

lm  <- read_seymour_octo_landmarks("seymour_octo_reg.csv")
con <- seymour_connectors("annotation:^all_somas$", conn = conn)
reg <- fit_seymour_octo_reg(lm, pos[, c("pre_pt_position_x", "pre_pt_position_y",
                                        "pre_pt_position_z")],
                            con[, c("x", "y", "z")], cv_folds = 5)
saveRDS(reg, "seymour_octo_reg.rds")

With the current 30 landmarks, the cross-validated error is about 3.6 µm.
